model: Regulated utility dividend capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management per-share EPS guidance (FY2026 $2.02-2.07, FY2027 ~$2.22-2.30, 9-11% consolidated through 2033), haircut; not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (13.9% 3yr / 14.8% 5yr) diverges more than 30% from revenue (4.4%) and EPS (4.7%) CAGRs. The equity series is total equity including Blackstone's noncontrolling interests ($2.4B) and ATM issuance, so it measures capital raised, not per-share compounding, and is rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 EPS -0.19). FCF CAGRs undefined: owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC) is negative in every year of the window (FY2022 -819, FY2023 -744, FY2024 -876, FY2025 -471), which is the capex program, not distress. Revenue is distorted by pass-through gas costs.

scenario_narratives.base: The base utility delivers the lower-middle of its 6-8% plan on tracker-recovered gas-main replacement and grid investment, and GenCo adds the guided increment on roughly the disclosed schedule: Amazon and Alphabet capacity ramps, the two 1,300 MW CCGTs reach commercial operation in 2030 without a further slip, and the Microsoft contract builds to 788 MW by 2031. Per-share EPS compounds about 8.5% a year from FY2026 to FY2033, at the low end of the 9-11% consolidated target, because the $40B plan needs steady ATM issuance and Blackstone-funded minority capital. The dividend follows earnings at a 58% payout. After 2033 the company is an ordinary rate-base compounder growing 3% with a 65% payout.
scenario_narratives.bull: Northern Indiana stays the preferred hyperscale corridor: Indiana policy stays supportive, further large-load customers sign onto the Pool Resource Assets, construction lands on budget, and the negotiated data-center returns come in above NIPSCO's regulated electric return as management intends. Per-share EPS holds the top of the 9-11% range through 2033 with dilution kept modest by Blackstone capital and customer prepayments, and the larger asset base supports 3.5% growth afterwards.
scenario_narratives.bear: One of three things goes wrong, and they are correlated: an AI-capex slowdown leads ADS to use its one-time option to halve committed capacity by 2032 or delays the Microsoft and Alphabet ramps; the first-of-scale CCGT and battery projects overrun or slip again past 2030 and trigger liquidated damages; or affordability pressure and a data-center backlash tighten rate-case outcomes in Indiana and Ohio. Capital is already committed, so the rating is defended with more common equity at lower prices, and per-share EPS growth falls to the bottom of the base-plan range and below. NiSource remains a solvent regulated utility in this case, it simply stops being a growth story.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NiSource is valued as what a shareholder receives: a dividend funded by regulated earnings, growing with per-share EPS, capitalised at an 8.25% cost of equity. Dilution from the equity-funded capital plan is charged once, through per-share growth. The regulated franchise makes the dividend stream durable; the question the model answers is how much to pay for the data-center growth layered on top, when the 10-year Treasury yields 5.15% and the stock trades at about 22x FY2026 earnings and 2.3x book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity is the largest lever: the stream is long-duration and the terminal value is most of the value, so each 0.5pt on the cost of equity moves the result by roughly 10%. The rate is built on a 5.15% 10-year yield; a fall in long rates would lift the value materially.

The FY0 anchor is GAAP FY2025 EPS ($1.95); adjusted FY2025 EPS is not in the extracted filings. This affects only the labelled year-1 growth rate, not the FY2026-27 EPS levels, which come from guidance.
EPS guidance and the 9-11% growth target come from earnings materials summarised in the Analysis JSON, not from the 10-K/10-Q text; the capital plan and ATM details are from the Q3-2026 10-Q.

Per-share guidance embeds management's own equity-issuance plan. If the plan needs more equity than assumed, the shortfall shows up as lower per-share growth (the bear path), not as a separate deduction.

Exit multiple: Gordon at the cost of equity gives roughly 13x terminal earnings against about 22x today. The model assumes multiple compression as growth normalises; holding today's multiple would roughly close the gap to the market price.
House and street bases coincide on this route because SBC is inside EPS; band_position carries no information.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 38.42-49.21
data_sources.financials: NI_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2008-FY2025 and quarters to Q3-2026); Q3-2026 10-Q for share count, ATM forward sales, debt, equity, dividend declared and the 2027-2033 capital plan
data_sources.qualitative: NI_Analysis.json (2026-11-15) for guidance, contracts and bull/bear axes

inputs.base_revenue_note: NOT sales. The engine's 'revenue' line is earnings attributable to common on the current fully diluted count: FY2025 diluted EPS $1.95 x 487.6M shares = $950.8M. Growth rates are therefore PER-SHARE EPS growth, so the dilution from the equity that funds the capital plan is already inside the path (management's EPS guidance is per share, after planned issuance).
inputs.share_count_basis: 479.67M shares outstanding at 2026-10-21 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) + 2.39M forward-sale shares settled October 2026 + 2.20M and 2.15M shares under the February and June 2026 ATM forward sale agreements (settle by December 2026) + ~1.2M LTIP dilution (diluted less basic average, ex forwards) = ~487.6M. Held FLAT: future equity issuance is charged once, through per-share EPS growth, not through a rising divisor.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at zero by construction: the flow is dividends to common, which are after interest, NCI distributions and reinvestment. Deducting the $18.2B of debt again would count it twice. Actual balance sheet at 2026-09-30 is in total_debt and cash.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 XBRL cash-flow add-back (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). No combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published. SBC is already an expense inside EPS, so the forward sbc_pct_path is 0 on this route and house and street bases coincide (band_position not meaningful).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta 0.65 x 4.75% ERP = 8.25%. Same rate in all three scenarios; hyperscaler concentration and construction risk are carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease cost ($301M of lease liabilities, FY2025) is inside net income, and net debt is not deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flow: EPS is after net income attributable to Blackstone's 19.9% interests in NIPSCO Holdings II and Generation Holdings II ($50.0M in 9M-2026). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. NiSource is a rate-regulated gas and electric utility in a capex supercycle ($40B planned for 2027-2033 against ~$3B of EBITDA). The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row; its governing principle is to discount the flow the business actually produces at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues, and it warns that reported FCF is structurally negative for infrastructure in a capex supercycle without that being a signal. Unlevered owner FCF is negative every year since FY2015 (FY2025 owner FCF -$471M) and will stay negative through 2033, so an owner-FCF DCF would rest entirely on a terminal value after a guessed capex normalisation. The flow that reaches shareholders is the dividend, funded by regulated earnings on rate base, so the model capitalises dividends per share at the cost of equity through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero (the same engine route as the REIT AFFO capitalisations). ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = earnings to common (per-share EPS x flat current share count); ebitda_margin 100%; capex_pct = earnings retention (100 - payout); D&A, tax, SBC and working capital 0 because EPS is already after all of them; FCF = dividends. Terminal payout of 65-67% with 2.5-3.5% growth is consistent with g = retention x ROE at an earned ROE near 10% (FY2026E EPS $2.055 on $19.96 book = 10.3%). FY0 CAVEAT: FY2025 EPS is GAAP diluted $1.95; the filings in Extracted/ carry no adjusted-EPS reconciliation, so year-1 growth bridges GAAP FY2025 to the adjusted FY2026 guidance midpoint of the narrowed range. last_fcf is recorded as true owner FCF (-420.0 - 50.9) for auditability and is NOT the base of this model. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. No buybacks; NiSource is a net issuer of equity (ATM program, $1.15B capacity left, expires December 2028).

bear.growth_note: FY2026 $2.02 (bottom of range), FY2027 ~$2.16 (base plan only, no GenCo contribution), then the bottom of the 6-8% base-plan range decaying to 3% as extra equity issued to defend the BBB+/Baa2 rating dilutes per-share growth. Dividend still grows, but slower than guided; payout drifts up to 67%.

base.growth_note: Per-share EPS: FY2026 $2.055 (upper half of the $2.02-2.07 guide), FY2027 $2.26 (midpoint of ~$2.22-2.30), then the low end of the 9-11% consolidated target fading to 7% by 2033 as GenCo capex rolls off after 2029, and to 4.5% by FY2035.
base.capex_note: capex_pct is earnings retention = 100 - dividend payout. Payout 58.4% in FY2026 ($1.20 on $2.055), held at 58% through the build (inside the 55-65% target), rising to 65% by FY2035 as growth slows.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.25% / 3.0% = 19.6x terminal dividend, about 12.8x earnings. The cap is on the dividend flow: 28x dividends = ~18x earnings at a 65% payout, the sector's long-run P/E. Gordon binds.

bull.growth_note: FY2026 $2.07 and FY2027 $2.30 (tops of both ranges), then the top of the 9-11% target sustained through 2033 on further large-load contracts filling the Pool Resource Assets; payout at the low end of the range (55%) while the build is at its peak.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 28x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the incremental growth rests on three hyperscale counterparties whose committed capacity exceeds the existing fleet, the returns are commercially negotiated rather than cost-of-service, and the CCGT date has already slipped once. Base 50%: guidance is specific, recently reaffirmed and backed by IURC-approved contracts. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs new contracts, on-budget first-of-scale construction and a stable Indiana policy environment all at once, for seven years.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
